newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ahern elected Irish Prime Minister on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Ahern elected Irish Prime Minister on Thursday.

text.p: Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern was on Thursday elected Prime Minister of a minority Irish government after winning the backing of Independents, including Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army.

Ahern won a parliamentary vote against outgoing Prime Minister John Bruton by 85 votes to 78 in the 166-seat parliament, overcoming the first electoral hurdle in what he promises will be a full five-year term.

He immediately named Charlie McCreevy, an opponent of high government spending, as Finance Minister and appointed party stalwart Ray Burke as Foreign Minister to handle the Anglo-Irish drive to find a Northern Ireland settlement.

Ireland's membership of the EU's economic and monetary union (EMU), a drive to cut taxes and crime and a solution to the 28-year Northern Ireland conflict will be the priorities of his government, officials said.
Ahern, Ireland's youngest premier, appointed his coalition ally Mary Harney as Deputy Prime Minister minister. It is the highest government office to have gone to a woman.
Harney, whose progressive Democrats won only four seats in June 6 elections against eight in the outgoing assembly was also appointed Minister of Enterprise and Employment.

But Ahern needed the backing of non-aligned legislators, including Caoimhghin O'Caolain, a legislator with Sinn Fein, the political voice of IRA guerrillas fighting British rule of Northern Ireland, to secure the Prime Minister's post.
O'Caolain said he would back Ahern in the parliamentary vote to find a successor to Bruton's centre-left coalition government.
Fianna Fail, which in common with other British and Irish parties refuses talks with Sinn Feun untilt he IRA calls a new ceasefire, said it did not seek the party's backing.
Other backers included Jackie Healy-Rae, an independent legislator for South Kerry, a rural backwater and a tourist idyll whose roads are acknowledged to be dreadful.

Rae, with his trademark cloth cap tucked in his blazer pocket, told the house that he expected Ahern to repair the roads in his constituency and even suggested, to laughter, that the entire car tax revenue be devoted to the project.
"Many of the best governments in this country have been minority governments," Ahern said after his appointment. He promised a "sound, stable and productive government".
Victory for Ahern's centre-right alliance in June 6 elections ended almost three years of the centre-left coalition of John Bruton.
Anglo-Irish plans to revive the Northern Ireland peace process are expected to be Ahern's first priority.
The initiative received a boost on Wednesday when Britain formally offered Sinn Fein a seat at Belfast peace negotiations if the IRA calls a ceasefire.
Burke will have responsibility for representing the Irish view in talks with Britain under the umbrella of a standing Anglo-Irish conference on the province.
McCreevy, 47, is seen as a tough-talking enemy of government spending who has already pledged to keep expenditure growth within four percent, two of which is for inflation.

He takes over an economy which is forging ahead and creating 1,000 jobs a week and will oversee the task of keeping the economy within the EU's Maastricht criteria so that Ireland can be among the first states to join EMU.
EMU is the goal of all major Irish parties and Ahern is on record as saying that his government will not change its mind despite the doubts of its biggest trading partner, Britain.
The formalities of forming a new government will be concluded on the first anniversary of the hit-man killing of Veronica Guerin, Ireland's most famous investigative reporter.

She is thought to have been ordered to be killed by a drugs baron she was investigating. One person has been charged with the crime and 186 questioned over an event which shocked the country and made it aware of the extent of organised crime.

A central pledge in Ahern's campaign was to introduce "zero-tolerance" methods of policing which would entail cracking down on every sort of crime to create a climate in which major offences would not be committed.
